subject: Science
chapter: Chapter 3: Interpreting Health: The Ultimate Treasure
central_question: How do physical, mental, social and environmental factors shape health, disease, prevention, immunity and responsible treatment?
in_scope_units: Health as complete physical, mental and social well-being, including the WHO definition and Indian health traditions.
Healthy habits, nutritious food, exercise, sleep, hygiene, clean surroundings, relationships and emotional well-being.
Signs and symptoms and the distinction between communicable and non-communicable diseases.
Pathogens, routes of disease transmission, vectors and preventive measures.
Lifestyle, environmental and nutritional causes of chronic and deficiency diseases.
Prevention through sanitation, immunity and vaccination.
Treatment, antibiotics, antibiotic resistance and responsible healthcare.
banned_topics: Detailed cell biology of microorganisms from Chapter 2.
Clinical diagnosis or individual medical prescriptions.
Unverified remedies or instructions to replace professional medical care.

known_pitfalls.claim: Health simply means not having a diagnosed disease.
known_pitfalls.correction: The chapter and WHO definition include physical, mental and social well-being.

known_pitfalls.claim: All diseases spread from one person to another.
known_pitfalls.correction: Communicable diseases can spread; non-communicable diseases such as diabetes and asthma do not spread between people.

known_pitfalls.claim: Symptoms and signs are the same.
known_pitfalls.correction: Symptoms are felt by the person, while signs can be observed or measured.

known_pitfalls.claim: Vaccines cure a disease after a person becomes ill.
known_pitfalls.correction: Vaccines are preventive and train the immune system before serious disease occurs.

known_pitfalls.claim: Antibiotics cure viral infections such as cold and flu.
known_pitfalls.correction: Antibiotics act against bacteria, not viruses or protozoa, and misuse promotes resistance.
